# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the open wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). It adds a ring of magnets so the phone snaps into the best charging position, with up to 15W of power. It was built with Apple's MagSafe technology as its base ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** (marketed as "Qi2 25W") is the newer version of the same standard. It raises the cap to 25W, nearly 70% more power than Qi2. The WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The first certified products appeared in July 2025.

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification for its magnetic charging. In practice:
- Apple's current MagSafe Charger is itself certified for Qi2 25W and ordinary Qi, so the gap between MagSafe and Qi2 is now mostly a matter of branding ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8)).
- Macworld notes that certified MagSafe chargers also have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, plus a magnetometer to prevent compass interference. In its tests, 15W MagSafe and Qi2 chargers charged at about the same speed ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).
- "MagSafe-compatible" chargers that aren't certified are usually just 7.5W with magnets, so they charge more slowly but are often cheaper (Macworld).

## What you actually get

| | Max power | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Uncertified "MagSafe-compatible" | ~7.5W | Magnets only |
| Qi2 / MagSafe (15W) | 15W | iPhone 12 and later |
| Qi2.2 / MagSafe 25W | Up to 25W | Needs a supported phone and a 30W+ adapter |

Which iPhones get the full 25W (per [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)):
- **25W:** iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max.
- **22.5W:** iPhone 16 and 16 Pro.
- **20W:** iPhone Air.
- **15W:** iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier.

Macworld's summary lumps the whole iPhone 16 and 17 lines together at 25W, so go by Apple's more precise numbers.

## Android

Few Android phones support Qi2. Per [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks):
- The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold charge at up to 15W.
- The Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at up to 25W.
- Samsung's Galaxy S26 lineup is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case to use Qi2 at up to 15W.

## Which should you buy?

- With an iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17 or 18 series, look for **Qi2.2 / Qi2 25W** or Apple's own charger, and pair it with a 30W+ adapter.
- With an older iPhone, a 15W Qi2 charger gives you the same speed for less money.
- You can check whether a charger is certified in the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

If you want the simplest option, the [Apple MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8) is certified for Qi2 25W. It's $49 for the 2 m version on Apple's page, and Macworld lists the 1 m at about $39. The power adapter is sold separately.

Tell me your phone model and I can narrow this down to specific chargers.
